paragraphs.en: Commander Reid Wiseman and his three crewmates were supposed to reach 219,667 nautical miles (252,788 standard miles, or 406,823 kilometers) — farther than any humans have ever traveled from their home planet — before turning back toward Earth on the sixth day of their 10-day mission to the moon.
paragraphs.zh: 指挥官里德·怀斯曼（Reid Wiseman）和三名队友本应在为期10天的奔月任务第六天抵达距地球219,667海里（252,788法定英里，即406,823公里）处——比任何人类从母星出发所到达的距离都更远——然后调头返回地球。

paragraphs.en: But the odometer on the Integrity spacecraft continued to tick upward as they shot past their intended point of return, leading the astronaut to fear that something had gone terribly wrong, he told an audience here at the Starmus VIII festival earlier this week. (This semi-annual event is held to celebrate achievements in science, exploration, and creativity.)
paragraphs.zh: 但“诚信号”（Integrity）飞船的里程表在他们飞过预定返回点后仍在继续攀升，这让这位宇航员担心出了严重问题，他本周早些时候在斯塔姆斯VIII节（Starmus VIII festival）上对听众说。（这一半年一度的活动旨在庆祝科学、探索和创造力领域的成就。）

paragraphs.en: "Mission control in Houston had told us our maximum distance would be 219,667 nautical miles and that was the furthest we were supposed to be from Earth," Wiseman said. "I was watching this number, and I saw it hit 219,667, and I thought, 'Great, this is the farthest we will be from Earth, and the next number I will see will be 219,666 ‪—‬ we'll be going home.' But about three minutes later, I didn't see 219,666; I saw 219,668. It went up. I was like. 'Huh? That's weird.'
paragraphs.zh: “休斯敦任务控制中心告诉我们，我们的最大距离将是219,667海里，那是我们预计离地球最远的位置，”怀斯曼说。“我一直盯着这个数字，看到它达到219,667，我想，‘太好了，这是我们离地球最远的时候，我接下来看到的数字将是219,666——我们要回家了。’但大约三分钟后，我看到的不是219,666，而是219,668。数字上升了。我当时想，‘嗯？这有点奇怪。’

paragraphs.en: "And then about three minutes later, it goes to 219,669, and that was the moment that I felt real fear because I thought we had just gone too far ‪—‬ we're never going to come home ‪—‬ and so I was very scared," he added.
paragraphs.zh: “然后大约三分钟后，数字变成219,669，就在那一刻，我感到了真正的恐惧，因为我以为我们刚刚飞得太远了——我们永远回不了家了——所以我非常害怕，”他补充道。

paragraphs.en: Then, at last, he saw the counter start to drop. Meanwhile, NASA astronauts Victor Glover and Christina Koch were at the window, doing science observations of the moon , and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen was sending reports back to mission control ‪—‬ so Wiseman's moment of terror went unnoticed.
paragraphs.zh: 然后，他终于看到计数器开始下降。与此同时，NASA宇航员维克多·格洛弗（Victor Glover）和克里斯蒂娜·科赫（Christina Koch）正在窗边对月球进行科学观测，加拿大航天局宇航员杰里米·汉森（Jeremy Hansen）正在向任务控制中心发送报告——因此怀斯曼的恐惧时刻无人察觉。

paragraphs.en: When Wiseman saw the odometer click back to 219,668 nautical miles, he said, "We're going home," and the crew let out a cheer. "I knew there was a good chance we might make it," he added.
paragraphs.zh: 当怀斯曼看到里程表跳回219,668海里时，他说：“我们要回家了”，机组人员欢呼起来。“我知道我们很有可能成功，”他补充道。

paragraphs.en: "Getting home safely is a testament to the engineering rigor and the flight control teams back here on planet Earth, who put this rocket together and then who controlled it as we went out to the moon and came back. Those are the true heroes of this mission. They have real courage."
paragraphs.zh: “安全回家证明了工程严谨性和地球上的飞行控制团队，他们组装了这枚火箭，然后在我们飞往月球并返回的过程中操控它。他们才是这次任务的真正英雄。他们拥有真正的勇气。”

paragraphs.en: The Artemis II mission launched from NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida on April 1. It was the first crewed flight of the Orion space capsule and the first crewed mission to travel to the moon since Apollo 17 in 1972, taking nearly 10 days to fly around the lunar far side and return to Earth.
paragraphs.zh: 阿耳忒弥斯2号（Artemis II）任务于4月1日从佛罗里达州NASA肯尼迪航天中心发射。这是猎户座（Orion）太空舱的首次载人飞行，也是自1972年阿波罗17号（Apollo 17）以来首次载人奔月任务，历时近10天绕月球背面飞行并返回地球。

paragraphs.en: Nearly every moment of the crew's activities in the Orion capsule was livestreamed to the world, garnering massive public interest in the mission. The Artemis II crewmembers were awarded the Stephen Hawking Medal for Science Communication at the Starmus VIII festival.
paragraphs.zh: 机组人员在猎户座太空舱内几乎每一刻的活动都向全世界直播，引发了公众对这次任务的巨大兴趣。阿耳忒弥斯2号机组人员在斯塔姆斯VIII节上被授予斯蒂芬·霍金科学传播奖（Stephen Hawking Medal for Science Communication）。
